### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 20  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.765)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:29557)

**Proposed mechanism:** NEXN (HGNC:29557) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030040); Regulation of actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030040) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cardiac muscle contraction (HP:0030170); Regulation of actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030040) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Loss-of-function mutations in NEXN disrupt the regulation of actin cytoskeleton organization, leading to both abnormal cardiac muscle contraction (a feature of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) and cardiomyopathy in general (as seen in MONDO:0013147).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NEXN with a gain-of-function mechanism or variants in unrelated genes that independently cause both MONDO:0013147 and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 20. _(variant: rs750374867)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of NEXN in cardiac function could lead to targeted therapies for both conditions, potentially by modulating actin dynamics or related pathways.

#### 2. cardiomyopathy, dilated, 2M  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.765)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:29557)

**Proposed mechanism:** NEXN (HGNC:7773) —DISRUPTS→ Nexilin function in cell adhesion and cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007155); Nexilin function in cell adhesion and cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Defective cell adhesion (HP:0030191); Nexilin function in cell adhesion and cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cytoskeleton organization (HP:0003694); Defective cell adhesion (HP:0030191) —LEADS_TO→ Dilated cardiomyopathy 2M (MONDO:0979243); Abnormal cytoskeleton organization (HP:0003694) —LEADS_TO→ Dilated cardiomyopathy 2M (MONDO:0979243). Loss-of-function mutations in NEXN disrupt nexilin function, leading to defects in cell adhesion and cytoskeletal organization. These cellular defects contribute to the pathogenesis of MONDO:0013147 and MONDO:00979243, ultimately manifesting as dilated cardiomyopathy.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in NEXN with a minor allele frequency greater than 1% in the gnomAD database would falsify the hypothesis that these variants are the sole cause of these rare diseases. _(variant: HGNC:7773)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of NEXN in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring nexilin function or mitigating the downstream consequences of its deficiency, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.
